methodology: Pre-processing retinal images by extracting the green channel, applying a Gaussian filter for smoothing, and generating feature images using four Gabor filters at angles of 90°, 45°, 0°, and −45°. The resulting filtered images are passed into a U-Net++ neural network featuring re-designed nested skip pathways, dense skip connections, and deep supervision to perform retinal blood vessel segmentation.
key_findings: The proposed method achieved superior performance on the MESSIDOR dataset. The re-designed nested skip pathways and dense skip connections in U-Net++ bridge the semantic gap between encoder and decoder sub-paths, facilitating easier optimization, improved gradient flow, and higher segmentation accuracy. The provided context does not state the specific numerical percentage by which U-Net++ improved accuracy over the original U-Net architecture.
